resources.string: Live speed-limit assistance with offline map data and advisory speeding-cost estimates.
Live speed-limit assistance with offline maps and advisory alerts.
Arrive safely. YouSpeed shows the detected speed limit live and indicates when fines, points, or driving-ban warnings may become relevant. YouSpeed can be wrong - keep your eyes on the road.
No offline road data is available until you download a map bundle in Settings.
Map data: Copyright OpenStreetMap contributors, ODbL 1.0. https://www.openstreetmap.org/copyright
Note: Displayed fines, points, and driving-ban information are advisory only and are not legal advice. Official notices and the law in force at the time are authoritative.

The fines, points, and driving-ban information shown in YouSpeed are advisory only. They are not legal advice or a binding legal assessment. Official notices and the law in force at the time are authoritative; additional fees and costs may apply.
Explore maps and features again when the recorder is stopped.
YouSpeed needs a downloaded map to show roads and speed limits. Use your location for a suggestion, or choose a region yourself.
Finding a map for your location…
No suitable location was found. Try again or choose a region below.
The download uses your internet connection, including mobile data. Afterward, the map works offline. Map data: OpenStreetMap contributors.
Allow precise location while using the app so YouSpeed can match your road and show your current speed. You can also choose spoken speed alerts.
Precise location is still required. Allow it in the permission prompt or open app settings and enable precise location.
Choose how far above the limit a spoken warning begins. Your existing settings are kept.
Record a drive as a video on this phone. Setup does not start recording or open the camera.
Start and stop on the driving screen

Tap the recorder button when you are ready. Its timer shows the session. Turn video off separately while keeping sign recognition or photos active. Camera permission is requested when you use the camera.

Open the video library after stopping. Tap a video to play it, use Share to send or upload it through another app, or select recordings to delete locally. YouSpeed keeps videos on this device; Panoramax uploads are for photos.

Android asks for camera permission when the camera is first started. This permission covers camera frames and video capture. Nothing is recorded during setup, and sign recognition without recording does not save video.
Your map and own corrections work without a camera. Camera recognition adds roadside signs.
The downloaded road data supplies known speed limits offline. A normal speed-limit sign has no camera eye. Map information may be missing or out of date.

Double-tap the speed-limit sign, then say the observed limit in German. Recognition runs on this phone and asks for microphone access when first used. Your confirmed correction stays local; review it in settings.

The camera can recognize roadside signs. An eye beside the active speed-limit sign means the displayed limit currently comes from camera recognition. When the camera assertion ends, the app returns to map data or your applicable correction. Always follow the signs on the road.
With recognition enabled, this option uses the camera on the driving screen without saving a dashcam video. You can also turn video off during a recorder session and keep recognition on.
Capture street-level photos with GPS while the recorder runs, even with video off. Photos stay on your phone until you choose to publish them on Panoramax.

Photos are captured at intervals during the recorder session. Stop the recorder, then open the photo gallery. Open a photo full-size and zoom to inspect it. Mark favorites to protect them from automatic cleanup. Select individual photos or all, clear the selection, or delete unwanted local photos.

Connect your Panoramax account in settings. Choose photos and confirm Upload to send the selected photos and their GPS locations for publication. Follow each batch’s progress, stop uploads when needed, and resume interrupted uploads. Uploads use your internet connection, including mobile data, and are available after recording stops.
You can change these choices in settings at any time. Finish setup to open the driving screen.
